discovery: The theory of cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmological density perturbations
motivation: Guth proposed that an early epoch of exponential expansion, driven by a scalar field, solves the horizon, flatness and monopole problems of the hot Big Bang. Linde turned this into a viable framework with new and chaotic inflation, showing how a slowly rolling field naturally ends inflation and reheats the universe. Mukhanov (with Chibisov) showed that quantum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed all cosmic structure, predicting a nearly scale-invariant spectrum with a slight red tilt. These sharp predictions — spatial flatness, adiabatic Gaussian perturbations, and a spectral index just below one — have been confirmed with remarkable precision by COBE, WMAP and Planck, with n_s ≈ 0.965 excluding exact scale invariance at high significance. Inflation transformed cosmology into a quantitative bridge between quantum field theory and the observed universe, and it frames today's central questions on the earliest moments of cosmic history.
